title: Spider-Man Almost Fought a Different X-Men Villain!
summary: Imagine you're writing a Spider-Man movie. You need a villain. But most of the famous ones are already used up! So the writers of 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' had to get creative. They thought about using a villain from the X-Men comics called the Shadow King. He's a creepy psychic (a mind-reader with powers) who jumps into people's bodies and controls them. The writers even had a cool idea: Spider-Man would only talk to him by phone at first, like in the movie 'Die Hard with a Vengeance.' But Marvel said no to that villain. So they picked Jean Grey instead — a powerful X-Men hero who can read minds. In the movie, she jumps between people and makes them do what she wants, kind of like the Shadow King would have. It's like if you planned a birthday party with a magician, but the magician couldn't come, so you got a juggler instead — and the juggler turned out to be amazing. The writers had to work around rules about which characters belong to which studio. In the end, Spider-Man got a villain from a whole different corner of the Marvel universe. Pretty wild, right?
why_it_matters: It shows that when your first plan doesn't work out — at school, in a game, or in a project — the backup plan can still turn out to be something you're proud of.

background_read: Marvel is the company that makes Spider-Man and the X-Men (a team of superheroes from Marvel comics), and it decides which characters are allowed to appear in which movie.
For a long time the X-Men movies were made by a different company, Fox, until Disney — Marvel's owner — bought Fox, which brought the X-Men back into Marvel's own movie world.
In the comics, the Shadow King is one of the X-Men's oldest enemies, a villain who fights with mind powers instead of strength.
Article_Structure: WHO: The writers of the movie 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', plus Marvel, which gets to approve which characters can be used.
WHAT: The writers wanted the X-Men villain Shadow King, but Marvel said no, so they used Jean Grey instead.
WHERE: Behind the scenes of a Marvel movie, where characters from different corners of the Marvel universe come together.
WHY: Because different studios own different characters, the writers had to find another villain who could still jump between people and control them.

perspectives.perspective: Writers who wanted the Shadow King
perspectives.description: They might be a little disappointed that Marvel said no to their first choice, but they kept the cool idea of a villain who jumps between people and controls them.
They are excited because a famous X-Men hero gets a big, scary role in a Spider-Man movie — a side of her that fans don't always see.
They have to protect their characters and follow the rules about which studio owns whom, even when the writers have a fun idea.
